text:
elaine: Quick follow-up to the recomposition RFC — trying to land a concrete paydown + rollout schedule for service splits. TL;DR: propose a 3-phase decomposition with clear ownership handoffs, a fast safety-rollback path, and a monthly tech-debt burn target. Looking for blockers and rough capacity estimates. :calendar:

sanjeev: +1 on the 3-phase idea. can you sketch the phases? curious about how we prevent cross-cutting KV cache regressions. :thinking_face:

maria: I flagged the KV cache risk in the RFC review — we need a compatibility shim for 2 quarters at least. otherwise we pay massive perf tax during transition.

elaine: agree. rough phases:
```
Phase 0 (1 month): prepare compatibility shim + runtime feature flags
Phase 1 (2 months): extract control-plane pieces (orchestration, rollout) into a new service; keep runtime in-place behind facade
Phase 2 (2 months): split KV cache ownership and migrate sessions incrementally by customer cohort
Phase 3 (1 month): consolidate observability & cut final facade, deprecate legacy endpoints
```
we're aiming for a 6-month horizon but can compress if we prioritize and accept some risk.

jack: timeline seems fine but we should bake-in a monthly tech-debt quota: e.g., 3 engineer-weeks/month dedicated to cleanup for the next 4 months. otherwise we keep accruing.

toni: +1 on quota. also need an explicit rollback plan per-phase. can we add an automated traffic switch with canary and instant revert?

elaine: yes — plan to use the routing layer to do canary by customer tag and auto-fallback to legacy service if error rate > 2% for 5m. that will be in Phase 1 test harness.

sanjeev: one implementation note: to avoid double-writes during migration we should prefer read-through from shim + write-through to both services for a bounded period. that'll require idempotency keys.

maria: idempotency is the right call. also encryption key rotation and audit logs need to be part of the migration checklist for Private deployments.

elaine: adding those to checklist. attached small migration checklist snippet: 
```
- feature-flag gate for new control-plane APIs
- compatibility shim for kv read path
- dual-write + idempotency validation harness
- canary traffic policy (customer tag) + rollback automation
- observability: per-route SLI + cost/latency dashboard
- security: KMS integration test (private) + audit enablement
```

jack: would like explicit owners for each checklist item. propose assigning per-squad and a single product engineer as the program lead.

elaine: assigned product lead = elaine, infra owner = sanjeev, runtime owner = jack, security = toni, migration QA = maria.

toni: will spin up a short-run load test to validate the compatibility shim's memory profile. ETA 2 weeks. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary test harness created for architecture/recompose - canary pipeline scheduled nightly.

maria: question: what's our target debt-paydown metric? lines of technical debt are fuzzy. i propose measurable target: reduce cross-service synchronous calls by 40% and remove 3 large debt endpoints in Quarter.

elaine: good measurable targets. final proposal for the doc:
- schedule: 6 months, phases as listed
- measurable debt targets: -40% sync calls cross-service, remove 3 endpoints, reduce peak p95 latency on enroll path by 15%
- monthly tech-debt hours: 3 engineer-weeks per team for 4 months
- rollback: automatic canary revert + gradable feature flags

sanjeev: logging: add correlation IDs across the shim so tracing stays intact during dual-write.

jack: ok to proceed with detailed RFC update + program plan? if no objections i'll create the project board and milestones.

maria: no objections from me.

toni: go ahead.

elaine: thanks everyone — i'll update the RFC and attach the migration checklist + owners. will post a short kick-off next week. :rocket:
